summary: Fail. The six ADV-P4B fixes of task 4.13t are implemented and pinned at HEAD 2fdb8f8. The judge verdict parse and the scorer decode the --format json event stream (judge-run.sh:919-938, review-score.ts:233-266). A future-dated or millisecond-scale last-good reading fails closed (quota.ts:374-380). The daemon guard matches argv tokens (review-run.sh:453, judge-run.sh:337). The KILL requires a recorded starttime (review-run.sh:499, judge-run.sh:383). The XDG call paths are guarded (review-run.sh:719-730, judge-run.sh:493-499). A hostile diff id refuses before the lock and any call (review-run.sh:364-369). Gates pass one file at a time: adversarial-p4b 12/12, review-score 25/25, review-run 65/0, and no fake or server process stayed behind. One blocking gap stays in the end-to-end contract: adjudicate.ts queue reads the stored raw outputs, which are event streams, without the decoder, so the adjudication of task 4.13 writes zero items and spec D11 silently degrades to a no-op. The gap does not block the 01:45 probe and night 1 of 2026-11-20: the timers are armed, the pilot set is complete with plain ids, the live last-good reading is fresh in seconds, and both drivers still parse every new refusal line.
blocking_findings: F1 (route to Green): The queue of task 4.13 reads the stored raw outputs without the event-stream decoder, so a real pass yields an empty adjudication. review-run.sh stores the unchanged stdout of `opencode run --standalone --format json` as the raw output of each diff (review-run.sh:757, 967, 1040-1041), so every stored <diff_id>.txt is an event stream. review-score.ts decodes it before the fence parse (decodeAnswerText at review-score.ts:233-260, called at 266), but the queue still parses the raw text: readFindings at adjudicate.ts:216-232, fed the raw file at adjudicate.ts:302-304. The fenced block inside a JSON-escaped event string never parses, so every real raw output returns null and the queue writes zero items. Proven with a node check: the verbatim queue readFindings on a {"type":"text","part":{"type":"text","text":"...fence..."}} stream returns null, and the same input through the review-score.ts decoder returns the findings. The failure is silent: judge-run.sh reads an empty queue and makes no call, apply writes an empty verdicts.json, review-score --verdicts counts no false claims and no real defects, and the task 4.13 verify clause 'each finding has a verdict of both judges, or it is left out' passes vacuously, so spec D11 degrades to a no-op and the 4.14 score file and review page show a wrong rank. Fix: copy decodeAnswerText into adjudicate.ts and call it in the queue readFindings, as judge-run.sh carries its own copy; pin it with a failing-first case in adjudicate.test.ts that feeds an event-stream raw output to the queue.
nonblocking_findings: N1: The new decoder of the scorer has no failing-first test. The Green commit touches no test file; adversarial-p4b.test.ts pins the judge-run.sh copy only (AJ1 at adversarial-p4b.test.ts:1532-1566), and every input of review-score.test.ts is a plain fenced block (fenced() at review-score.test.ts:194-196; the 16 fixtures under harness/model-guide-tests/fixtures/review/outputs/ are plain text). Remove decodeAnswerText from review-score.ts and all 25 scorer tests still pass, so the ADV-P4B-1 fix for the scorer is unpinned. The next Red round should add a scorer pin and the queue pin of F1.

N2: The plan row 4.13t presents ADV-P4B-1 as the decode of 'the judge verdict parse and readFindings of the scorer' (measure/tracks/model_guide/plan.md:2403-2413) and names two of the three consumers of the raw outputs. The third consumer, adjudicate.ts queue, reads the same files (adjudicate.ts:16-19, 302-304) and holds no decoder (F1). Correct the row when F1 closes, so the event-stream contract names every consumer.
evidence: Contract 1, the stored raw output: review-run.sh:757 runs `opencode run --standalone --format json` and review-run.sh:1040-1041 moves the unchanged stdout to <OUT_DIR>/<diff_id>.txt, so the stored raw output of a pass is the event stream. The scorer reads the decoded answer text: review-score.ts:233-260 (decodeAnswerText) and 265-266 (readFindings calls it); review-score.test.ts gives 25 passed (25) at HEAD. The queue and score schemas are unchanged: the queue shape sits at adjudicate.ts:350-363 in a file the range does not touch, the pass record keys at review-score.ts:531-549 and the route record keys at 463-472 are the documented shapes. The page inputs of task 4.14 still work: leak-check.ts, preview.sh, and guide.ts are untouched by the range (git diff --stat 56ab786..2fdb8f8 lists 5 files), and guide.ts reads state, date, score, and blocker_recall, which the diff does not change.

Contract 1, the queue: adjudicate.ts queue does NOT read the decoded answer text. readFindings at adjudicate.ts:216-232 parses the raw text for the fence, and writeQueue feeds the raw file at adjudicate.ts:302-304. Node proof at the audited HEAD: the verbatim queue readFindings on a real-shaped {"type":"text","part":{"type":"text","text":"...```json ... ```..."}} event stream prints null, and the same input through the review-score.ts decoder prints the findings. So every real raw output contributes no item and queue.json holds no groups. This is F1.

Contract 2, the refusal lines and exit codes: diff id, 'review-run: a diff id holds a parent segment' and 'review-run: a diff id is not a plain id' (review-run.sh:364-369) through refuse at review-run.sh:122-126, exit 2; pinned by AM1 (exit 2, one stdout line, no model call, no pass record; adversarial-p4b.test.ts:1250-1283). XDG folders, 'review-run: the job HOME is outside the job root' and 'the job <sub> folder is outside the job root' (review-run.sh:719-730, judge-run.sh:493-499 with the same words), exit 2; pinned by AH1 (data symlink, review-run), AD3 (home symlink, review-run), and AD4 (home symlink, judge-run), each asserting exit 2, one named line, no call, and no record. Last-good quota, quota.ts:374-380: an age below -60 s gives state stopped with the reason 'the last-good reading is dated in the future'; the tool exits 0 with one 'quota: <reason>' stderr line; pinned by AQ1 (a reading ten years in the future) and AQ2 (a millisecond-scale fetchedAt) through expectStopped. In a probe a stopped quota refuses with 'review-run: the probe refused: the quota state is stopped: ...' exit 2 (review-run.sh:681-682); in a pass it writes a record with state open and exits 0 (review-run.sh:689-692).

Contract 3, the drivers, read only and never run: probe-4.10.sh:53-79 and night-4.11.sh:88-117 read the Go quota themselves through `timeout 90 "$BENCH_RA_QUOTA" status --json` and parse windows['5h']['percent'] and windows['weekly']['percent'], so the quota.ts change adds no new driver line. Every new runner line keeps the shapes the drivers parse: a refusal is one 'review-run:' line with exit 2, which probe-4.10.sh:139-142 records as '$route refused $out exit=$rc' and night-4.11.sh:203-228 tolerates while it reads the state from the newest pass record; the stopped reason of the new quota guard flows through the unchanged probe_refuse and record paths. The pass-record glob of the night driver (night-4.11.sh:213-218) matches the runner derivation byte-for-byte (review-run.sh:380-384, 566: tr -cs 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '-' and sha256sum | cut -c1-12). The reachable and done lines of the probe are unchanged.

Contract 4, the probe answer: nothing of this diff blocks the 01:45 probe and night 1 on 2026-11-20. Verified: systemctl --user list-timers holds mg-probe-4-10b.timer at Fri 2026-11-20 01:45 +07 and mg-night-4-11-n1.timer at Fri 2026-11-20 02:00 +07, and both units ExecStart the driver scripts in the jobs folder. heavy-run.sh and ra-quota exist and are executable (/home/daniebo/Desktop/advantage-pr/scripts/jobs/, ra-quota updated 2026-11-19 05:02). The pilot set mg-2026-11p is complete in the private store: 6 diffs, 6 keys, 6 messages under forge-01..03 and mono-01..03, all plain ids, so the new diff-id guard cannot refuse the real sets (the public set mg-2026-11a holds plain ids too). The runner creates its own job folder each run, so the XDG guard passes in the driver path. The live last-good reading is fresh and in seconds (/tmp/ra-quota-lastgood.json fetchedAt 1795048839.47, age 163 s at 07:42 +07), so the new skew guard does not trip. Both drivers export BENCH_RA_QUOTA and RA_QUOTA_LASTGOOD (probe-4.10.sh:16-17, night-4.11.sh:16-17). The F1 queue gap lands on task 4.13 after the passes, not on the probe or night 1.
